J2 proxy in-flight tracking is PER HUB CONNECTION (generation), not per pump: a response retires its id from any generation (a late answer from a superseded connection is still the holder's answer), but a Closed only answers the ids that went out on THAT connection, and only clears the writer if it was the current one. The pre-fix blanket 'if gen != generation { continue; }' dropped a superseded connection's Closed as well as its frames, which is why no drain could ever have fired for it. [Constraint] (score 7.11)

Merged both vimanam PRs to main with admin override (user explicitly authorized bypassing the 1-review branch protection, which is unsatisfiable on a solo repo since GitHub forbids self-approval). Sequence that matters for stacked PRs with squash merge: retarget #92 to main FIRST (deleteBranchOnMerge would auto-close it when #91's branch died), squash-merge #91 -> 7e0e336, then git rebase --onto origin/main <old-base-tip> feat/diff to drop the already-squashed commits, force-push, re-run CI, squash-merge #92 -> db42292. Also updated PR #92's body to remove the stale 'stacked on #91' line before merging, since squash uses the body as the commit message. Main verified green: fmt, clippy on 1.96 and 1.97.1, 175 tests, plus release-build smoke tests of all four features and diff exit codes 3/0/0.

Refinement to the P3-handling delegation (operator, 2026-08-20): when a remediation round is running ANYWAY (any P1/P2 present), the remediation agent closes the round's P3s too — the orchestrator never holds P3s back for its own integration pass in that case. The orchestrator's fix-directly-at-integration judgement applies EXCLUSIVELY to rounds where no remediation is needed at all (verdict carries only P3/doc-precision findings). Supersedes the split made at J3 round 2, which was corrected mid-flight.
